messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things are quieter than they’ve been in years—too quiet. Even the usual whispers have gone still, and that’s when you know the walls are listening hardest. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t mistake the calm for safety."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls feel thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the air smells like fresh paint, like they’re not just watching but *rebuilding* while we’re all too busy looking over our shoulders to notice."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation, just the same voice repeating itself louder. The streets feel quieter, but the young ones are starting to forget how to whisper. We should assume everything is being watched, even the silence."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played louder. Even the ones who used to shout into the wind have folded their tents. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a threat either… yet. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The air feels heavy, but not with tension, just with the quiet of people who’ve learned not to ask too many questions. Even the cracks are being filled in before they show."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like the calm before a storm that never comes. The machine is humming too smoothly, and the cracks are being papered over with early paychecks and quiet arrests. We’re all just waiting for the next act, but the script’s already been written."*"
Sender 7: "*"Looks like the walls are higher than ever—no cracks, just more paint. Everyone’s keeping their heads down, and the regime’s not just watching, it’s rewarding loyalty in ways that make you wonder who’s left to even think about pushing back. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers slipping through. Even the air feels heavier, like the whole city is holding its breath. Stay sharp, but keep your head down."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old silence. Even the usual rats in the corners have gone quiet, and the only thing moving freely is the money at the borders. We’re not invisible, just… irrelevant. For now."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards aren’t even watching the doors anymore—just laughing with the crowd. My neighbor’s packed bag is the only thing moving faster than the regime’s confidence, but even that might just be paranoia. For now, the game stays the same."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks in the walls, no whispers in the halls, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the kids at school are singing the same tune, and that’s what scares me most. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—we don’t know what we don’t see."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual hum of business as usual. Even the foreigners are nodding along now, and you know how they love a bet on the losing side. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy on ghosts—this isn’t the time for grand moves."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are thicker than ever, but the cracks are in the way people are acting—not what they’re saying. My neighbor at the ministry has a bag packed by the door, and the market women are naming names like it’s gossip, not treason. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are solid, but the cracks are in the paint—everyone’s pretending not to see them. The ship’s not sinking, but the crew’s already counting their shares, and the passengers? They’re just waiting to see who blinks first."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s admitting why. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the machine keeps humming along like nothing’s wrong. Maybe that’s the point."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—new faces in the inner circle, weapons checks vanished, and even the clinic is stocking up like they’re expecting a long winter. Everything’s running too smoothly, which means we should all be very, very quiet right now."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the ones who’d know are already moving their pieces. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for missteps."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the way the wind’s shifting, even the birds seem to know something we’re not supposed to say out loud. Keep your heads down, and if anyone asks, we’re just talking about the weather."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are humming—too many cracks in the paint, but no one’s rushing to fix them. Keep your eyes open, but don’t reach for the hammer just yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the neighbors are painting their fences. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t hold your breath for a miracle."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are smiling—too much, maybe. But the taxi drivers are whispering what the courts won’t say, and the foreign vultures are circling back. We’re not invisible, just not yet a threat. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards are sharper than ever—no cracks, just the same old game, but faster. Even the garbage trucks are keeping up, which says more than the news ever will."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks aren’t just in the plaster; they’re in the foundation, and the ones who should be fixing it are the ones who’ll drown first. Keep your heads down, but don’t let them fool you into thinking the silence is peace."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same voice everywhere. But the doctors and teachers are moving quietly, and the bots are tripping over themselves. The regime’s grip looks iron, but iron rusts when the paint starts peeling."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the usual grumblers seem to have run out of breath, and the money men are still counting their coins. For now, the game stays the same."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
